ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $AB\parallel CD$, $\angle A=45^\circ$, $\angle C=\angle E$, what is the measure of $\angle C$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB\parallel CD$ and $\angle A=45^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle DOE=\angle A=45^\circ$\\
Given that $\angle C=\angle E$ and $\angle C+\angle E=\angle DOE$,\\
we have $\angle C=\frac{1}{2}\angle DOE=\frac{1}{2}\times 45^\circ=\boxed{22.5^\circ}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, points A, O, and E are located on the same approximately horizontal straight line, with O between A and E; points C, O, and D are located on the same oblique line, with O between C and D; ray AB is drawn from A toward the upper right, and ray CD is drawn from C through O toward the upper right, and the figure gives AB ∥ CD. Triangle COE is formed by line segments CO, OE, and CE, and OD is the extension line of OC, so ∠DOE is the exterior angle of triangle COE at point O. Reasoning: Because AB ∥ CD, and AE/OE is the transversal, the angle ∠A formed by AB and AE is equal to the corresponding angle ∠DOE formed by CD and OE. It is known that ∠A = 45°, so ∠DOE = 45°. In triangle COE, exterior angle ∠DOE is equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles, that is, ∠DOE = ∠C + ∠E. It is also known that ∠C = ∠E. Let ∠C = ∠E = x, then 2x = 45°, solving gives x = 22.5°. Therefore ∠C = 22.5°.

The small triangle to use is triangle COE, with the exterior angle at O formed by OD and OE. From the text, use AB ∥ CD and ∠A = 45°. Since AE/OE is a transversal to the parallel lines AB and CD, the angle between OD and OE equals ∠A, so ∠DOE = 45°. In triangle COE, ∠DOE is an exterior angle, so ∠DOE = ∠C + ∠E.
